clue.text: Be dubbed utterly ignorant!

definitions.meaning: to be dubbed is to be made a knight with a tap of the sword, i.e. to be knighted
living in mental darkness, quite without knowledge or enlightenment

explanation.surface: An exclamation that someone given a new title must be a complete dunce.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a pun: BE KNIGHTED, said out loud, matches the answer exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Benighted literally means overtaken by night, and figuratively unenlightened or ignorant; 'be dubbed' is the punning 'be knighted'.

clue.text: Pussyfoot on stage in one of these

definitions.text: Pussyfoot on stage in one of these

parts.words: Pussyfoot on stage in one of these
parts.note: the pantomime cat of the fairy tale wears a famous pair of footwear, so the stage puss puts its foot in one

explanation.surface: Someone treading cautiously in a theatre, wearing some kind of shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: Puss in Boots is a fairy tale and a popular British Christmas pantomime; 'Pussyfoot' is split into puss's foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat in the pantomime Puss in Boots has its feet in this footwear.

clue.text: Getting irritated, demanded about a pound

indicators.note: about places the word for demanded around the pound sign

parts.note: demanded means needed, required
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone growing annoyed after being asked for roughly a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Needled means provoked or annoyed, as by repeated small jabs; the definition is read as a past participle, 'got irritated'.

clue.text: Comprehensive strike in which the winner takes all

definitions.meaning: in baseball, a home run with all bases loaded, or a sweeping knockout blow

definitions.text: in which the winner takes all
definitions.meaning: in bridge or tennis, winning every trick or every major title

explanation.surface: A general strike described as a contest where the victor gets everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand slam is a sweeping blow in baseball and, in bridge or tennis, a clean sweep of every trick or title.

clue.text: Twist Charon's tail for bragging

indicators.note: to twist is to contort, so the letters of the ferryman's name and tail are wrung into a new order

parts.note: Charon is the ferryman of the dead in Greek myth; the S of the possessive is used too

explanation.surface: Instructions to wrench the mythic ferryman's tail as punishment for boasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' rearranges CHARONS plus TAIL; the S of 'Charon's' counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrasonical comes from Thraso, the boastful soldier in Terence's comedy, and means vainglorious.

clue.text: Demand payment for a horse of this colour

definitions.meaning: to press a debtor persistently for money owed
a dull greyish-brown coat colour in horses

explanation.surface: A creditor asks for money in return for a horse of some shade.
explanation.definitionFit: To dun is to pester a debtor; a dun horse is greyish-brown.

clue.text: It sounds like a bridle-path

parts.note: bridle sounds like bridal, and the path a bride walks in church is the passage between the pews

explanation.surface: A remark that something resembles a track for horse riders.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride walks up the central passageway of a church between the pews, a bridal path.

clue.text: This sounds like Private Eye's language!

indicators.note: this sounds signals that the words before the definition are to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: like is as, and a private eye is a 'tec, short for detective

explanation.surface: A remark that something resembles the jargon of a satirical British magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a British satirical magazine, but here a private eye is a detective, a 'tec; 'as 'tec' spoken matches the name of the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Aztec is a name for Nahuatl, the tongue of the Aztec people of Mexico.

clue.text: Prevent from entering such a bid

definitions.meaning: to keep someone out by closing the door
in bridge, a high pre-emptive bid meant to stop opponents bidding

explanation.surface: An attempt to stop someone getting in by making a certain offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut out is to exclude; a shut-out bid in bridge is a pre-emptive call.

clue.text: Giving a black look the way he does, perhaps

definitions.text: Giving a black look the way he does, perhaps

parts.words: Giving a black look the way he does, perhaps
parts.note: make-up darkens the lids; and a private eye follows people, so 'he' is a detective tailing someone

explanation.surface: Someone scowling in the same manner as some man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black look' suggests scowling, but it means dark make-up; 'he' is a private eye, who shadows people.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye-shadow is cosmetic colouring for the eyelids, and a private eye's job is to shadow suspects.

clue.text: Outdoor opera in resort

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, so these letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: An opera performed at a seaside holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place but means re-sort: the letters of OPERA IN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air events take place outside rather than under a roof.

clue.text: Japanese button set to go off in A-bomb

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for an atomic weapon

parts.note: an atomic bomb is a nuke

indicators.note: go off suggests exploding, so the letters of set are scattered

explanation.surface: A Japanese device timed to explode inside an atomic bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To go off' rearranges SET to ETS, which goes inside NUKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A netsuke is a small carved toggle worn on a Japanese sash to secure a pouch, so a kind of button.

clue.text: Only daughter — probably well-heeled too!

parts.note: only means sole, single

explanation.surface: An only daughter who is likely rich as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-heeled' looks like rich, but here it is a shoe with a heel, so also given its sole.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe that has been heeled has likely been resoled too at the cobbler's.

clue.text: A sorry outfit?

parts.note: sorry means repentant, not shabby: the coarse garment worn as a sign of penance

explanation.surface: A remark about a shabby set of clothes or a poor organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitents traditionally wore coarse sackcloth and ashes to show remorse.

clue.text: Borgia and weird sister in race

parts.note: Cesare Borgia was the Renaissance Italian prince
the weird sisters are the three witches in Macbeth

explanation.surface: A Borgia and a strange sibling competing in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cesarewitch is a long-distance handicap horse race run at Newmarket in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cesarewitch is an annual flat handicap held at Newmarket racecourse.

clue.text: Finish part of the game on the green

definitions.text: part of the game on the green
definitions.meaning: in lawn bowls, a stage of play in which all the woods are bowled in one direction

explanation.surface: Completing a stage of a game played on grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawn bowls, played on a flat grass green, is divided into ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To end is to finish; an end is a single round of play in bowls.

clue.text: One in show business, or supporter of show?

definitions.meaning: someone who displays goods or animals at a show, or a cinema owner who screens films
one who backs a show by putting things on display

explanation.surface: A question whether someone is a performer or a patron of a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibitor puts things on public display, at a trade fair or by screening films in a cinema.

clue.text: Settled about performing G and S-how wise

indicators.note: about puts the word for settled around the others

parts.note: settled, as a bird lands, means lighted (alighted)
on means performing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: A remark on the wisdom of staging Gilbert and Sullivan operettas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'G and S' looks like Gilbert and Sullivan, but it gives just the letters G and S, placed after ON inside LIGHTED; 'how' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-sighted figuratively means far-seeing, prudent and wise about the future.

clue.text: Mug up the language, and stick with it!

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then turned
Arabic is a language

explanation.surface: Advice to cram a foreign language and persevere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug up' looks like cram, but 'up' reverses MUG; 'stick with it' is something to glue with.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum arabic is a natural gum from acacia trees used as an adhesive.

clue.text: Rash fellow has a murmur about! reform

indicators.note: reform means form again, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A reckless man, with a heart murmur, needs to change his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform' rearranges HAS A MURMUR plus C.
explanation.definitionFit: A harum-scarum is a reckless, impetuous person.

clue.text: Anarchist press, infuriating to City people

parts.note: red is a term for a revolutionary or radical
rags is slang for newspapers

explanation.surface: Radical newspapers that enrage London financiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, where bulls are investors; a red rag infuriates a bull. The definition reads as a noun phrase, things infuriating.
explanation.definitionFit: A red rag to a bull is a provocation, and stock-market bulls are City people.

clue.text: This marble would be turned brown by New York

indicators.note: would be turned brown by means that adding the next words would make a colour, so they are taken off it

parts.note: tawny is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A marble going brown from the city's grime.
explanation.walkthrough: TAW plus NY would make TAWNY, a shade of brown; take NY from TAWNY.
explanation.definitionFit: A taw is a large playing marble, used as the shooter.

clue.text: Metal wrapping -the solution can baffle

parts.note: a can is a tin
to baffle a plan is to foil it

explanation.surface: Something baffling about a metal container.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinfoil is thin metal sheet used for wrapping food.

clue.text: Associate is a sleeping partner

definitions.meaning: literally, someone who shares one's bed

explanation.surface: A business associate described as an inactive investor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeping partner' is a British term for an investor who takes no active role; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedfellow is literally one who shares a bed and figuratively an associate or ally.

clue.text: Hardy appears briefly under English national character

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts this piece below the other

parts.note: Thos is the short form of Thomas, the novelist Thomas Hardy's first name

explanation.surface: The novelist turns up briefly beneath English national identity.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the distinctive spirit or character of a people or culture.

clue.text: Career in charge of funny old characters

parts.note: to career is to rush along, to run

explanation.surface: A dash run by a person managing some odd old people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' are not people but letters: runes, the old Germanic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Runic means relating to runes, the angular letters of ancient Germanic alphabets.

clue.text: Wood-notes at the start of Rigoletto

parts.note: C, E, D and A are musical notes

indicators.note: at the start of picks the first letter of Rigoletto

explanation.surface: Woodwind notes at the opening of Verdi's opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood-notes' looks like woodwind music, but the hyphen splits into the definition 'Wood' and four notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedar is a fragrant timber from coniferous trees.

clue.text: Helping to ignite a cheroot in a coach

indicators.note: a helping is a portion, so a portion of the words that follow gives the letters

explanation.surface: Lighting a cigar for someone while riding in a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a vehicle but means a tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is an instructor or tutor, one who teaches.

clue.text: Short title is The Turn of the Screw, perhaps

definitions.meaning: an abbreviated form of Reverend, a clergyman's title

definitions.text: The Turn of the Screw, perhaps
definitions.meaning: a revolution, one turn of something rotating, abbreviated

explanation.surface: A remark that the Henry James novella has a brief name.
explanation.walkthrough: The Turn of the Screw is a Henry James story, but here it is literally one turn, a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Rev abbreviates both Reverend, a clergy title, and revolution, a single rotation.

clue.text: This paper is small, so concentrate

definitions.text: This paper is small, so concentrate

parts.words: This paper is small, so concentrate
parts.note: a compact newspaper format; the word also once meant a compressed tablet, a concentrated form

explanation.surface: An instruction to read carefully because the print is tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: The word began as a trademark for compressed medicine tablets, hence small and concentrated.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a small-format newspaper, the term derived from a brand of compressed tablets.

clue.text: They sprinkle flowers

definitions.meaning: the perforated nozzles on watering cans that scatter water
thorny blooms of the genus Rosa

explanation.surface: Blossoms that scatter something.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose is the sprinkler head of a watering can, and also a classic garden bloom.

clue.text: University student more than half way through compiling archive of transport

indicators.note: places the next letters well past the midpoint of the rearranged word
compiling means putting together, so the letters of archive are assembled anew

parts.note: L, the learner plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A college student partway through putting together a transport archive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compiling' rearranges ARCHIVE to VEHICAR; U and L go in after its fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehicular means relating to vehicles, the means of transport.
